title: Short-term effects of various NSAIDs on Danio rerio embryos
author: Chabchoubi, Bouchhima, et al.
materials: The following chemicals purchased from Sigma-Aldrich (Deisenhofen, Germany) were used for the exposure of zebrafish embryos: Diclofenac (99.0 to 101.0% dried substance (ds)), ibuprofen (98.5 to 101.0% ds), ketoprofen (99.0 to 100.5% ds) and Paracetamol (99.0 to 101.0% ds). CAS numbers and other characteristics of the selected drugs are shown in Table 1 (http://www.drugbank.com). All chemicals were dissolved in AW without any auxiliary solvent.

During all experiments, the exposure media were changed once a day. For each concentration, 3 samples before (0 h) and 3 samples after exposure of 24, 48, 72 and 96 h, were collected prior the renewal of the exposure solution. In order to pinpoint any possible changes of the nominal concentration, the stability of the drugs in the exposure solutions was monitored during the four days experiment using a JENWAY 7315 spectrophotometer with 1-cm cuvette path length slot in the wavelength range of 200 – 350 nm. All stability tests were performed during 5 days and using the highest concentration of each NSAID (11.25 mg/L). After 24 of exposure the solution was renewed and the exposure was continued for 24 h more. This operation was repeated five times.

steps.title: Dissolve chemicals in AW
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amounts of Diclofenac (purity 99.0‑101.0 % ds), Ibuprofen (98.5‑101.0 % ds), Ketoprofen (99.0‑100.5 % ds) and Paracetamol (99.0‑101.0 % ds) (all from Sigma‑Aldrich, Deisenhofen, Germany) and dissolve each directly in aquarium water (AW) without any auxiliary solvent to obtain stock solutions; the highest test concentration will be 11.25 mg L⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare exposure solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the stock solutions with AW to the desired test concentrations for the zebrafish embryo assay; ensure each exposure vessel contains the correct concentration (e.g., 11.25 mg L⁻¹ for the highest level).

steps.title: Set up embryo exposure
steps.instruction: Place Danio rerio embryos into the exposure vessels containing the prepared NSAID solutions, following the OECD TG 236 guidelines for embryo handling.

steps.title: Renew media and collect samples daily
steps.instruction: Once per day, before changing the exposure solution, collect three replicate samples of the exposure medium (time 0 h) and, after the 24‑h exposure period, collect three replicate samples again (at 24, 48, 72 and 96 h). Then completely replace the exposure solution with fresh NSAID‑containing AW. Repeat this renewal operation five times (total of five days).

substeps.instruction: At each time point (0, 24, 48, 72, 96 h) take three replicate aliquots before renewal.
After the 24‑h exposure, take three replicate aliquots.
Discard the used solution and add fresh exposure solution of the same concentration.

steps.title: Measure drug absorbance for stability
steps.instruction: For each collected sample, measure absorbance using a JENWAY 7315 spectrophotometer equipped with a 1‑cm cuvette, scanning the 200‑350 nm range. Record absorbance at the drug‑specific maxima: 275 nm (Diclofenac), 225 nm (Ibuprofen), 260 nm (Ketoprofen) and 250 nm (Paracetamol). Plot calibration curves of concentration versus absorbance to assess any deviation from the nominal concentrations over the 5‑day period.
